production.note: US model years. Petrolicious: 'for 1994, Mazda upgraded the powerplant to a 1.8-liter engine'. End (provisional): Edmunds lists a 1997 MX-5 Miata with the 1.8 L (edmunds-1997-miata, database), Petrolicious treats 1997 as the NA's final model year, and Mazda says the next generation 'debuted in 1998 as a 1999 model year' (mazda-nao-miata-25).

body.note: Two-seat roadster with no fixed-roof version.

displacementL.note: 'a 1.8-liter engine'; Edmunds 'Engine Size 1.8 L' (edmunds-1994-miata). No opened page gave the cc figure.

aspiration.note: No forced induction is mentioned; inferred.

transmission.note: Petrolicious: 'either a five-speed manual or the much rarer four-speed automatic'.

powerHp.note: PROVISIONAL (single article plus databases). Quote (Petrolicious, Khris Bharath): "for 1994, Mazda upgraded the powerplant to a 1.8-liter engine with 128 horsepower and a much sturdier differential." Edmunds 1994: "Horsepower 128 hp @ 6,500 rpm" (edmunds-1994-miata); KBB 1994: "128 @ 6500 RPM" (kbb-1994-miata). From 1996 the rating was 133 hp (Edmunds 1996 and 1997: "133 hp @ 6,500 rpm", edmunds-1996-miata, edmunds-1997-miata). Reference year is the launch year 1994; 128 hp and 133 hp each cover two model years.

weightLb.note: PROVISIONAL (databases). 1994 '2dr Convertible', 5-speed manual. Quote (Edmunds): "Curb Weight 2,293 lbs." KBB 1994 'Convertible 2D' agrees: "Curb Weight: 2293 lbs." (kbb-1994-miata). Edmunds prints the same figure for 1996 and 1997, so the databases do not show any year-to-year change.
